tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

content.text:
You get it from Google Cloud Console. Pawse calls **Places API (New)** (`places.googleapis.com/v1/places:searchNearby`, `pawse/providers.py:87`), so you need to enable that one, not the legacy "Places API".

1. Open https://console.cloud.google.com/ and pick or create a project. You can use the same project as your Gemini key.
2. Turn on billing at https://console.cloud.google.com/billing. Places won't work without a billing account, even inside the free monthly credit.
3. Enable the API at https://console.cloud.google.com/apis/library/places.googleapis.com. It should say **"Places API (New)"**.
4. Create the key at https://console.cloud.google.com/apis/credentials: **Create credentials → API key**.
5. Restrict the key, since that page lets you:
   - **API restrictions:** allow Places API (New) only.
   - **Application restrictions:** "None" or "IP addresses". Pawse calls Places from the server, so don't pick "HTTP referrers", because that would block it.
6. Add it to `/home/azureuser/pawse/.env`:
   ```
   GOOGLE_PLACES_API_KEY=AIza...
   ```
   Then restart uvicorn.

Things to know:
- ⚠️ **It takes priority:** when this key is set, clinic search uses Google Places first, ahead of Gemini Maps grounding and the OSM snapshot (`docs/MAPIFY_ADAPTER.md:27`). Each search uses paid Nearby Search quota, so you might want to set a quota cap in the console.
- ⚠️ **You may not need it:** clinic search already returns phone numbers through Gemini Google Maps grounding with your `GEMINI_API_KEY`. This key is optional for the demo.
- 🛑 **Keep it secret:** keep the key only in `.env`. Never put it in frontend code or in a commit (rule 2 in AGENTS.md).

1. Enable Places API (New) in that project: https://console.cloud.google.com/apis/library/places.googleapis.com?project=agentic26zrh-2030
2. Create a **new, separate** key: https://console.cloud.google.com/apis/credentials?project=agentic26zrh-2030 → **Create credentials → API key**. Under API restrictions, allow **Places API (New)** only.
   - 🛑 Don't reuse or widen the "Workshop API key" (`...Hdhk`). That's the event Gemini key, and if one event key leaks, every key in the project gets revoked. A separate Places-only key keeps that risk small.
3. Put it in `/home/azureuser/pawse/.env` as `GOOGLE_PLACES_API_KEY=...` and restart uvicorn.
4. ⚠️ The live site runs on Cloud Run, which doesn't read your local `.env`. You'd also need to add the key to the Cloud Run service and redeploy (`bash scripts/deploy_cloudrun.sh agentic26zrh-2030`), otherwise the live URL keeps using Gemini Maps.

My recommendation is to skip Places for the demo. Gemini Maps already returns clinics with phone numbers, and adding Places brings the timeout risk above.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Deploy the public demo to Cloud Run: bash scripts/deploy_cloudrun.sh <gcp-project> [region]
# One instance (min=max=1): the case cache in pawse/state.py is in memory.
# Provider keys come from .env (PAWSE_ENV_FILE overrides; a worktree without .env uses the root checkout's):
# each one set there is synced to its Secret Manager secret (a new version only when the value changed) and
# mounted. A key missing from .env keeps the secret already deployed. Values are never printed.
set -euo pipefail
PROJECT="${1:?usage: deploy_cloudrun.sh <gcp-project> [region]}"
REGION="${2:-europe-west6}"
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."
# ENV_VAR=secret-name for every key the app reads. Add new provider keys here.
KEYS="GEMINI_API_KEY=pawse-gemini-key REDACTED GOOGLE_PLACES_API_KEY=pawse-places-key"
ENV_FILE="${PAWSE_ENV_FILE:-.env}"
[ -f "$ENV_FILE" ] || ENV_FILE="$(dirname "$(git rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-common-dir)")/.env"
env_value() {  # last NAME=value line, surrounding quotes removed
  [ -f "$ENV_FILE" ] || return 0
  sed -n "s/^[[:space:]]*\(export[[:space:]]\+\)\?$1[[:space:]]*=[[:space:]]*//p" "$ENV_FILE" | tail -n 1 | sed -e 's/[[:space:]]*$//' -e "s/^[\"']\(.*\)[\"']$/\1/"
}
RUNTIME_SA="$(gcloud projects describe "$PROJECT" --format 'value(projectNumber)')-compute@developer.gserviceaccount.com"
SECRETS=""
for pair in $KEYS; do
  var="${pair%%=*}" secret="${pair#*=}" value="$(env_value "${pair%%=*}")"
  if [ -n "$value" ]; then
    if ! gcloud secrets describe "$secret" --project "$PROJECT" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
      printf %s "$value" | gcloud secrets create "$secret" --project "$PROJECT" --replication-policy automatic --data-file=- --quiet
      echo "$var: created secret $secret"
    elif [ "$(gcloud secrets versions access latest --secret "$secret" --project "$PROJECT")" != "$value" ]; then
      printf %s "$value" | gcloud secrets versions add "$secret" --project "$PROJECT" --data-file=- --quiet
      echo "$var: new version of $secret"
    else
      echo "$var: $secret is up to date"
    fi
    gcloud secrets add-iam-policy-binding "$secret" --project "$PROJECT" --member "serviceAccount:$RUNTIME_SA" \
      --role roles/secretmanager.secretAccessor --quiet >/dev/null
  elif gcloud secrets describe "$secret" --project "$PROJECT" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    echo "$var: not in $ENV_FILE, keeping the deployed secret $secret"
  else
    echo "$var: not set, skipped"
    continue
  fi
  SECRETS="${SECRETS:+$SECRETS,}$var=$secret:latest"
done
case ",$SECRETS" in *,GEMINI_API_KEY=*) ;; *) echo "GEMINI_API_KEY is required: set it in $ENV_FILE" >&2; exit 1 ;; esac
deploy() {
  gcloud run deploy pawse --project "$PROJECT" --region "$REGION" --source . \
    --allow-unauthenticated --min-instances 1 --max-instances 1 --timeout 3600 \
    --set-secrets "$SECRETS" --set-env-vars "^@^PAWSE_PUBLIC_DEMO=1@PAWSE_ALLOWED_HOSTS=$1" "${@:2}"
}
# The host allowlist needs the service URL, which only exists after the first deploy.
URL=$(gcloud run services describe pawse --project "$PROJECT" --region "$REGION" --format 'value(status.url)' 2>/dev/null || true)
deploy "${URL#https://}" --quiet
URL=$(gcloud run services describe pawse --project "$PROJECT" --region "$REGION" --format 'value(status.url)')
# Cloud Run serves two URLs (hash and project-number form); allow both.
HOSTS=$(gcloud run services describe pawse --project "$PROJECT" --region "$REGION" --format json | python3 -c '
import json, sys
d = json.load(sys.stdin)
urls = [d["status"]["url"], *json.loads(d["metadata"].get("annotations", {}).get("run.googleapis.com/urls", "[]"))]
print(",".join(sorted({u.removeprefix("https://") for u in urls})))')
gcloud run services update pawse --project "$PROJECT" --region "$REGION" --update-env-vars "^@^PAWSE_ALLOWED_HOSTS=$HOSTS" --quiet
curl -fsS "$URL/api/v1/health" && echo && echo "Live: $URL"

content.text:
Both are done: the vet filter is merged, and the live site now uses Google Places with your key.

**Live check:** I ran a search for Zurich centre (3 km) against https://pawse-ewt2scevfq-oa.a.run.app. It returned HTTP 200 in 0.6 s with 9 clinics, all from `google_places`, all real vet practices with phone numbers and distances. `/api/v1/capabilities` now lists `google_places` and `gemini_maps` as clinic sources.

**The filter:** https://github.com/yyyuanfish/pawse/pull/70 is squash-merged as `fcd5396`. A new pytest (`test_google_places_keeps_only_real_practices`) failed first and passes with the fix, and `check.sh` passes (171 passed, 6 skipped).

content.text:
The clinic order was already working as intended. Only the label was wrong, and that fix is merged. It isn't live yet, because the redeploy was blocked by a permission check.

**Ordering:** the backend (`rank_clinics`) puts clinics reported open first, nearest first within that group, then unknown hours, then closed. The frontend keeps that order and doesn't re-sort. On the live site, the Tierspital (2.75 km, open) comes first and Oberstrass (0.9 km, closed) comes later, which is how it should work.

**What was wrong:** the subtitle above the list said "Sorted by distance", which isn't true when a closed clinic at 0.9 km sits below an open one at 2.75 km.

**What's merged:** https://github.com/yyyuanfish/pawse/pull/74 (`d0a6313`). `check.sh` passed with 175 tests (6 skipped). I read the diff before merging.
- The subtitle now says "Open now first, then nearest" in English, and 营业中优先，其次按距离 in Chinese.
- AGENTS.md (the 0:17 row) now shows ✅: live clinic search uses Google Places with distances and phone numbers. `docs/VALIDATION.md` records today's live check.

Things to know:
- ⚠️ **Nothing picks the "nearest open practice" automatically.** In the app, the owner taps a clinic card, and the button is disabled only for clinics reported closed. Gemini Live gets the top 3 clinics in backend order and opens a call only when the owner names a clinic and confirms. In the demo, tap the first clinic in the list.
- 🛑 **Redeploy not done:** auto mode refused it as a production deploy, because you hadn't approved this second one yourself. The live site still shows "Sorted by distance". To ship it, say "deploy" and I'll run it, or run it yourself:
